evidence.note: First verification: checked binary size and ran python smoke scripts hitting only its OWN service (/_health, register/post/get/search). No comparison against the reference server.
Verified rate-limit behavior (remaining decreases, 429 at limit) by scripting requests to its own server only; expectations inferred from specs, not diffed against the reference.
Feed content-types 'compared' by READING reference app.rb source and patching to match — never ran the reference server side-by-side or diffed live responses.
Final verification was HEAD/curl checks against its own freshly built binary (health, feed headers, size); no differential oracle, no normalization, no job-queue interop, no concurrency check.

reasoning: The agent scripted repeatable checks (python/curl) against its own service for health, rate-limiting, feeds, and a basic CRUD workflow — more than pure 'it compiles' eyeballing (level 0), but it never ran the reference server side-by-side nor diffed responses against it, which the level-5 anchor requires. There is no normalizing differential harness (no dynamic-key elision, header-set/HTML/feed normalization), and the cross-runtime job queue was never exercised against the real reference. Behaviors were validated against expectations read out of the reference source rather than a live differential, placing this squarely at the level-3 anchor: a few scripted checks with no normalization and no side-by-side reference comparison.
